message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
The example uses the **gcloud CLI** (the easiest way to interact with the Compute Engine API) but I also include the equivalent **REST‑API JSON payload** so you can call it directly from your own code if you prefer.

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You have a Google Cloud project (`PROJECT_ID`) with billing enabled.  
> * The Compute Engine API is enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You have the `gcloud` CLI installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * You have the **NVIDIA GPU driver** installed on the instance after boot (see note at the end).

---

## 1. Using the gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### Optional: Startup script to install NVIDIA drivers

Create a file named `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver (Ubuntu 20.04)
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470
# Reboot to activate the driver
sudo reboot
```

Make sure the script is executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

> **Tip:** If you want to use a different GPU count or machine type, just change the variables above.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a custom application), here’s the JSON body you would POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Endpoint** (replace `{project}` and `{zone}`):

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
```

**Headers**:

```
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
```

> **Note:** The `acceleratorType` path includes your project ID because GPU types are project‑specific.

---

## 3. After the instance boots

Once the instance is running, SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone us-central1-a
```

Verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

## 4. Common pitfalls & troubleshooting

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **GPU not available in zone** | Check `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="zone:(us-central1-a)"` to confirm availability. |
| **Instance fails to start** | Inspect the serial console logs via `gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output`. |
| **Driver not installed** | Ensure the startup script is correctly referenced (`--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh`). |
| **Billing quota exceeded** | Verify GPU quota in the GCP console under “IAM & Admin → Quotas”. |

---

### Quick reference

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `gcloud compute instances create …` | Create instance via CLI |
| `gcloud compute instances list` | List instances |
| `gcloud compute instances delete INSTANCE_NAME` | Delete instance |
| `gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output` | View serial console logs |

Feel free to copy the snippets into your scripts or adapt them to your workflow. Happy GPU computing!
